Find the nearest decision boundary for a single target observation

bl_find_local_cf.Rd

Searches across multiple eigenvector pairs for the closest decision boundary to the target observation in the rotated biplot space. For each pair, the loading matrix is rotated so that the target observation lies along the first rotated axis, then a fine grid is scored and the boundary contour is extracted.

Usage

bl_find_local_cf(
  bl_result,
  bl_target,
  set_filters = NULL,
  max_pairs = 10L,
  m = 200L,
  distance = c("mahalanobis", "euclidean"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

bl_result

A "bl_result" object.

bl_target

A "bl_target" object from bl_select_target.

set_filters

A "bl_filters" object from set_filters, or NULL (no actionability constraints).

max_pairs

Integer; maximum number of eigenvector pairs to try. Default 10L.

m

Integer; grid resolution along each axis. Default 200L.

distance

Character; cross-pair selection metric. One of "mahalanobis" (default) or "euclidean". See Cross-pair selection criterion section above.

verbose

Logical; print progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

A list of class "bl_local_result" with the following fields:

B_z

1 x 2 matrix; best boundary point in rotated Z-space.

B_x

Data frame (1 row); back-projected boundary in X-space.

B_pred

Scalar predicted probability at the boundary.

dist_z

Euclidean distance from target to boundary in Z-space (reported for all pairs).

dist_mahalanobis

Squared Mahalanobis distance from target to boundary in X-space (reported for all pairs).

distance

Character; the selection metric used ("mahalanobis" or "euclidean").

Z_target

1 x 2 matrix; target coordinates in rotated Z-space.

best_pair

Integer vector of length 2; winning eigenvector pair.

Vr_rot

p x 2 rotated loading matrix for the best pair.

tVr_rot

2 x p inverse loading matrix for the best pair.

Z_train_rot

n x 2 matrix; training data in rotated Z-space.

Zgrid

Grid coordinates in rotated Z-space.

grid_prob

Numeric vector of model scores at each grid point.

col_value

Colour vector for grid points.

ct_local

Raw contour list from grDevices::contourLines.

xseq, yseq

Grid axis sequences.

min_val, max_val

Grid axis limits.

all_distances

Named numeric vector; Z-distance per pair tried.

all_distances_mahalanobis

Named numeric vector; squared Mahalanobis distance per pair tried.

solution_found

Logical.

blocking_constraint

Character message if no solution, else NULL.

bl_target

The "bl_target" object.

bl_result

The "bl_result" object.

set_filters

The "bl_filters" object passed in, or NULL. Stored so that bl_find_sparse_cf can identify "fixed" variables and revert them to their observed values.

Rotation

The rotation adapts Biplot_rotation() from the research script (scripts/1.3 Optimal Rotation.R). An SVD-based orthogonal rotation matrix \(A\) is computed such that the rotated loading matrix aligns the target observation with the projection plane defined by proj_pair. This gives each eigenvector pair the best possible chance of revealing a nearby boundary.

Constraints

The Z-space training hull polygon is not applied here because the per-pair rotation invalidates the polygon from bl_build_grid(). Two constraint types are applied instead:

train_ranges

Back-projected X-space values must lie within the per-variable ranges observed in the training data.

set_filters

Actionability constraints supplied via set_filters.

Cross-pair selection criterion

The best eigenvector pair is selected by minimum distance from the target to the nearest valid boundary vertex. Two distance metrics are available:

"mahalanobis" (default)

Squared Mahalanobis distance in the original X-space using the within-class covariance matrix \(W\) stored on bl_result$metric_inv: \(d_M^2 = v^T W^{-1} v\) where \(v = B_x - x_{obs}\). This is invariant to the eigenvector pair chosen and is the mathematically sound default – it measures within-class noise units regardless of which 2D rotated slice produced the counterfactual.

"euclidean"

Plain Euclidean distance in the rotated 2D Z-space: \(d_z = ||Z_{target} - B_z||_2\). Not comparable across pairs (each pair captures a different amount of variance), but preserves the pre-Mahalanobis behaviour for reproducibility.

Within-pair selection (the nearest valid contour vertex) always uses 2D Euclidean distance in the rotated Z-space; only the cross-pair comparison is affected by distance.
